review_notes: I read the whole target file. I read unitResidueFourier and its Parseval theorem in ResidueFourierParseval.lean, and I grepped the other uses of complexResidueMean. In Mathlib I checked Finset.expect and Fintype.expect_eq_sum_div_card, and the expect form of Cauchy–Schwarz. unitResidueFourier uses stdAddChar(h*r), a different sign convention from ZMod.dft. I judged it a deliberately different representation and did not report it. The one finding is a moderate-confidence candidate: complexResidueMean looks like an avoidable duplicate of 𝔼, and I could not rule out that the divide-by-φ form was chosen on purpose for the manuscript. I did not report the theorems themselves as duplicates, since the rubric excludes standalone theorem duplication.

findings.problem: complexResidueMean is the uniform average of v over the finite group (ZMod q)ˣ. Mathlib already has this concept as Finset.expect, written 𝔼 r, v r. Fintype.expect_eq_sum_div_card gives (∑ i, f i) / Fintype.card ι, and ZMod.card_units_eq_totient identifies the card with φ(q). The file's own Cauchy–Schwarz step goes through the sum form (sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq plus manual card/totient simp). Mathlib's expect-form Cauchy–Schwarz, Finset.expect_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq, would match the mean directly. Downstream files unfold the definition each time instead of using expectation lemmas. SampledHistogram.lean does this with `simpa only [complexResidueMean,sum_sub_distrib,sub_div,unitResidueFourier,...`, and ProjectedHistogram.lean does it with `rw [complexResidueMean,manuscriptProjectedValue_eq_sum]`. This gives a private averaging notion that none of the expectation API (linearity, constants, norm bounds) applies to without unfolding.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the name complexResidueMean as a thin abbreviation, but define it as `𝔼 r, v r` (Finset.expect over univ). Add one bridging lemma, `complexResidueMean v = (∑ r, v r) / (q.totient : ℂ)`, proved from Fintype.expect_eq_sum_div_card and ZMod.card_units_eq_totient. Then restate complexResidueMean_square_le and the later linearity steps with the Mathlib expectation lemmas (expect_sub_distrib, expect_const, expect_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq) instead of unfolding to ∑/φ. Alternatively, keep the definition and prove only the bridging lemma `complexResidueMean v = 𝔼 r, v r`, so Mathlib's lemmas can be used downstream.
findings.benefit: The averaging notion becomes the standard one, so Mathlib's Cauchy–Schwarz and linearity lemmas apply without repeated unfolding to a sum divided by φ. The projection-contraction proofs get shorter, and readers see at once that this is an ordinary mean. The name complexResidueMean and the existing statements stay usable.
